resource.name: aws_dynamodb_table_replica
resource.description: Provides a DynamoDB table replica resource for DynamoDB Global Tables V2 (version 2019.11.21). Use lifecycle ignore_changes for replica in the associated aws_dynamodb_table configuration. Do not use the replica configuration block of aws_dynamodb_table together with this resource as the two configuration options are mutually exclusive.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource enables the creation and management of replicas for DynamoDB Global Tables V2, facilitating multi-region data replication and high availability. It is commonly used to set up globally distributed applications requiring low-latency access to data across multiple AWS regions. Key configurations include lifecycle management with `ignore_changes` for replica settings and ensuring compatibility by avoiding mutual exclusivity with the `replica` block in the `aws_dynamodb_table` resource.

examples.title: Basic Example
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource to create a cross-region replica of a DynamoDB table using the `global_table_arn` argument. It showcases the use of multiple AWS providers for region-specific configurations, the `ignore_changes` lifecycle block to manage replica updates, and tagging for resource organization.

arguments.name: deletion_protection_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether deletion protection is enabled (true) or disabled (false) on the table replica.
arguments.llm_summary: The `deletion_protection_enabled` argument for the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to control whether deletion protection is enabled on the table replica, preventing accidental deletion when set to `true`. This configuration is typically used to safeguard critical data replication setups, aligning with lifecycle management and disaster recovery goals.

arguments.name: global_table_arn
arguments.description: (Required) ARN of the main or global table which this resource will replicate. Optional arguments:
arguments.llm_summary: The `global_table_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the primary or global DynamoDB table that the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource will replicate. By setting this required argument, users enable the creation of a replica table in a different AWS region, supporting multi-region redundancy, data synchronization, and improved application availability.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the replica table resource, enabling precise referencing and management within Terraform configurations. While optional, setting this argument can help users track and organize replica instances, especially in complex multi-region deployments.

arguments.name: kms_key_arn
arguments.description: (Optional, Forces new resource) ARN of the CMK that should be used for the AWS KMS encryption. This argument should only be used if the key is different from the default KMS-managed DynamoDB key, `alias/aws/dynamodb`. Note: This attribute will not be populated with the ARN of default keys.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_arn` argument for the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to specify a custom AWS KMS Customer Master Key (CMK) ARN for encrypting the replica table, overriding the default KMS-managed DynamoDB key (`alias/aws/dynamodb`). By setting this argument, users can achieve enhanced control over encryption, aligning with specific security or compliance requirements for data protection in distributed environments.

arguments.name: point_in_time_recovery
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable Point In Time Recovery for the table replica. Default is `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `point_in_time_recovery` argument for the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to enable or disable Point In Time Recovery (PITR) for the replica table, providing the ability to restore data to any point within the last 35 days. This feature is typically used to enhance data durability and recovery capabilities, supporting disaster recovery and compliance requirements.

arguments.name: table_class_override
arguments.description: (Optional, Forces new resource) Storage class of the table replica. Valid values are `STANDARD` and `STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS`. If not used, the table replica will use the same class as the global table.
arguments.llm_summary: The `table_class_override` argument in the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to specify the storage class for the replica table, overriding the default class inherited from the global table. By setting this argument to either `STANDARD` or `STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS`, users can optimize storage costs or performance based on their access patterns and data retention needs.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to populate on the created table. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument allows users to define a map of key-value pairs to assign metadata to the DynamoDB table replica, enabling resource categorization, organization, and cost allocation (e.g., by environment, team, or project). When specified, these tags override any matching keys set at the provider level, ensuring granular control over tag management for the replica resource.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags inherited from both the resource-specific tags and any provider-level default tags. This enables centralized tagging for resource organization, cost allocation, and governance, ensuring consistent metadata across the replica table for tracking and management purposes.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block for the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform should wait for the creation of a DynamoDB table replica to complete. By configuring this timeout, users can control the behavior of long-running operations, ensuring Terraform does not prematurely fail during replica provisioning in distributed environments.

arguments.name: delete
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string, e.g., "30m") Terraform will wait for the deletion of a DynamoDB table replica to complete. Configuring this timeout ensures predictable behavior during resource destruction, helping users manage lifecycle operations and avoid prolonged or stalled delete processes in their infrastructure.

arguments.name: update
arguments.llm_summary: The `update` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string, e.g., "30m") Terraform will wait for updates to the replica table to complete. Configuring this timeout helps manage long-running update operations, ensuring Terraform does not prematurely fail during replica modifications in distributed environments.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_dynamodb_table_replica` resource defines customizable time limits for operations related to creating, updating, or deleting a DynamoDB table replica. By configuring this block, users can manage operation durations to prevent long-running tasks from stalling infrastructure workflows, ensuring better control over resource provisioning and lifecycle management.
